site.social.choose.familyalbum.text: FamilyAlbum if you want a family album with nothing to set up: it's free with ads, keeps your photos in its own cloud, and its paid plan adds longer videos.

site.social.choose.meta.text: Instagram or Facebook if you want to reach a wide audience or follow public accounts: they're free and everyone is already there, in exchange for ads, a ranked feed and public posts used to train Meta's AI unless you object.

site.social.choose.otc.text: Off The Cloud if you want a private place for your family and friends that nobody else owns, with your photos and files backed up at home on the same small device.

site.social.choose.pixelfed.text: Pixelfed if you want a public, ad-free Instagram alternative on the fediverse, and are happy to join a server or run one yourself.

site.social.choose.whatsapp.text: WhatsApp if you mainly want to chat: messages and calls, with photos that arrive in a chat rather than an album and live only on the phones.

site.social.compare.checked.text: Checked in October 2026. The other services' details come from their own help and policy pages, linked below.

site.social.compare.lead.text: How each one handles your photos and your family's privacy, as their own pages describe it.

site.social.compare.title.text: Off The Cloud compared with Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, FamilyAlbum and Pixelfed

site.social.diff.address.text: Everyone has an account on a device. Each person in the feed has an account on an Off The Cloud device, their own or yours, with an off-the.cloud address. The bridge account that gives the addresses is free for two years, then €9.99 + VAT a year.

site.social.diff.messenger.text: No private messages, on purpose. With no chats or direct messages, there's less room for bullying or for a stranger to approach a child: what people share is posts and comments, and only with the friends they accept.

site.social.diff.middle.text: Nobody in between. Your posts are on your device, and your friends' devices fetch them from it. Our bridge relays the connection and keeps none of what passes through, so there's no company server holding everyone's photos.

site.social.diff.no_ads.text: No ads, no algorithm, no AI training. Nothing is sold, nothing ranks your feed, and nothing you post is used to train AI models.

site.social.diff.title.text: What's different from the big apps

site.social.faq.cost.a.text: The software is free and open source. You need a Raspberry Pi 5 and two USB drives, bought once, and an off-the.cloud address for everyone in the feed: the bridge account is free for its first two years, then €9.99 + VAT a year with up to five addresses, shared by your device and the family accounts you give one; for more, write to us.

site.social.faq.fediverse.a.text: No. Off The Cloud devices only talk to each other: your posts never appear on the fediverse, and you can't follow fediverse accounts from it. That's part of what keeps it private: your posts are never public, and there's no search for strangers to find you with.

site.social.faq.fediverse.q.text: Does it work with Mastodon, Pixelfed or the fediverse?

site.social.faq.library.a.text: No. Friends see only what you post in the feed. Your photo library, your files and the other accounts on your device stay private: a friend's device can only fetch the photos and videos of your posts.

site.social.faq.library.q.text: Can my friends see my photo library?

site.social.faq.messages.a.text: On purpose, to make the network safer, for children above all. Without chats or direct messages, there's less room for bullying or for a stranger to approach a child: what people share is posts and comments, and only the friends someone accepts see their posts or can comment on them. Nobody can be found by searching, either: there's no directory and no suggested friends, so a friend request needs the exact address.

site.social.faq.messages.q.text: Why are there no private messages?

site.social.get.alerts.text: Notifications that matter. Your phone tells you when someone accepts your friend request, likes or comments: nothing designed to keep you scrolling.

site.social.get.backup.text: Your photos, already safe. The same device backs up every phone in the family in full resolution and keeps your files, so what you post is already backed up at home.

site.social.get.family.text: Room for the whole family. Give each person an account on your device, with their own address, photo library and password, and be friends with each other in the feed.

site.social.get.feed.text: A feed of the people you know. Photos and videos, several to a post, with a caption, comments and likes, newest first. Nothing suggested and nothing sponsored.

site.social.get.leave.text: You decide what stays. Delete a post or a comment and it goes from your friends' devices too. Remove a friend and you can delete everything they shared with you, and ask their device to delete what you shared there.

site.social.get.links.text: Links for everyone else. Send a collection to the grandparents as a link that expires: they open it in their browser, with no account or app, and can download the originals.

site.social.hero.lead.text: Off The Cloud is free, open-source software that gives your family a social network of its own. You post photos and videos, comment and like, and only the friends you accept see them. Each family keeps its posts on its own small device at home, a Raspberry Pi 5, and friends' devices share them with each other, so no company holds your photos, shows you ads or decides what you see. The same device backs up your phones and keeps your files.

site.social.start.accounts.text: Add the family. In Settings › Users, in the web app or the phone apps, add an account for each person with Request bridge access on, and choose a first password to give them. They change it in Settings › Change Password, and from then on only they know it.

site.social.start.device.text: Set up the device. The computer app prepares the Raspberry Pi 5's card, and you finish the setup from your phone over Bluetooth, in about 20 minutes. It asks for a bridge account, which gives your device its off-the.cloud address.

site.social.start.friends.text: Add friends. In Friends, type the name of a friend's device, such as casa for casa.off-the.cloud, and send the request. Once they accept, your posts appear in each other's feed.

site.social.start.links.text: Share with everyone else. Choose photos in Images, add them to a collection and share it as a link.
